name: policy-prefetch-failure
description: A8 harness: does aggressive prefetching help the mean and hurt the tail? Run once as filed (predictive_prefetch) and once with --policy hot_cold using the same seed; the hypothesis is that growth-anticipation prefetching raises the local-hit ratio but its extra install traffic queues behind demand on the tight link and raises p99. This is a hypothesis to verify, not a result. It is not a measured-hardware experiment.
assumptions: Local capacity is intentionally 2 GiB so the working set churns and every policy decision is exercised; a real node has far more DRAM.
Prefetch parameters are deliberately aggressive (degree 4, high in-flight cap) to expose the contention failure mode if it exists.
Prefetches share the demand fabric with no priority lane, so prefetch traffic visibly competes with demand fetches.
The workload is synthetic KV-cache decode, not a captured serving trace; arrival rate is raised versus phase1-overflow to keep the link loaded.
Values are starting presets from docs/HARDWARE-MODELS.md. Replace them with measured values before making absolute claims.

provenance.source: docs/HARDWARE-MODELS.md local DRAM preset, capacity overridden for this test
provenance.method: Latency and bandwidth use the local DRAM preset. Capacity is deliberately reduced to 2 GiB so the decode working set cannot fit and policies must churn.
provenance.notes: Test fixture, not a deployment configuration.

provenance.method: Accelerator count and memory capacity from the product class. tokens_per_second intentionally omitted.
CXL.mem class latency and per-port bandwidth; not measured and not fitted to a switch topology.
One-way latency and sustained bandwidth for a CXL.mem class link; queue depth and in-flight limits are scenario assumptions.
